agencies.description: The Office of Management and Budget coordinates development of the President’s budget, oversees agency performance and management, and reviews regulations, legislative proposals, and executive actions for fiscal and policy coherence.

agencies.name: Office of Manufactured Housing Programs (OMHP)
agencies.description: The Office of Manufactured Housing Programs regulates the design and construction of HUD-code manufactured housing, enforces installation and consumer protection standards, and oversees dispute resolution and retailer certification programs.

agencies.name: Office of Minority Health (OMH)
agencies.description: The Office of Minority Health leads HHS efforts to improve health outcomes for racial and ethnic minority populations through policy development, partnerships, and programs that advance health equity and culturally competent care.

agencies.name: Office of Multifamily Housing Programs (MFH)
agencies.description: The Office of Multifamily Housing Programs administers FHA multifamily mortgage insurance, rental assistance contracts, and asset management for federally assisted housing portfolios through a national network of HUD field offices.

agencies.name: Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP)
agencies.description: The Office of National Drug Control Policy coordinates development and implementation of national drug control strategy, aligns federal agency efforts, and supports data-driven prevention, treatment, recovery, and supply-reduction programs.

agencies.name: Office of Natural Resources Revenue (ONRR)
agencies.description: The Office of Natural Resources Revenue collects, accounts for, and disburses revenue from energy and mineral production on federal and American Indian lands and the Outer Continental Shelf under applicable laws and agreements.

agencies.name: Office of Nuclear Energy
agencies.description: The Office of Nuclear Energy advances research, development, and demonstration on nuclear energy technologies to improve reactor safety, security, economics, and waste management in support of clean energy and national security goals.

agencies.name: Office of Personnel Management (OPM)
agencies.description: The Office of Personnel Management administers civil service policies for the federal government, operates health and retirement benefits programs, maintains hiring systems and personnel records, and supports agency human capital management.

agencies.name: Office of Policy Development and Research (PD&R)
agencies.description: The Office of Policy Development and Research produces data analysis, policy evaluations, and research publications that inform HUD strategies on housing markets, community development, homelessness, and fair housing.

agencies.name: Office of Postsecondary Education (OPE)
agencies.description: The Office of Postsecondary Education administers federal student aid policy, international education programs, and institutional eligibility to expand access to high-quality postsecondary education and strengthen global higher-education engagement.

agencies.name: Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)
agencies.description: The Office of Refugee Resettlement funds states and partners to deliver transitional assistance, social services, and specialized care that promote stability, health, and self-sufficiency for refugees and other eligible populations.

agencies.name: Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
agencies.description: The Office of Science and Technology Policy advises the President and coordinates federal science and technology policy across agencies on research priorities, innovation ecosystems, STEM education, and emerging technology risks.

agencies.name: Office of Scientific and Technical Information (OSTI)
agencies.description: The Office of Scientific and Technical Information preserves and disseminates the results of Department of Energy-sponsored research and development through digital repositories, data products, and open science services.

agencies.name: Office of Servicemember Affairs
agencies.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s Office of Servicemember Affairs monitors military consumer financial issues, coordinates with stakeholders, and advances policies and education that protect service members, veterans, and military families.

agencies.name: Office of Special Counsel (OSC)
agencies.description: The Office of Special Counsel investigates prohibited personnel practices, enforces the Hatch Act’s political activity rules for covered employees, and protects federal whistleblowers who disclose waste, fraud, and abuse.

agencies.name: Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS)
agencies.description: The Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services administers special education formula grants, vocational rehabilitation programs, and disability research investments that support students, job seekers, and state systems.

agencies.name: Office of Surface Mining, Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE)
agencies.description: The Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement regulates surface coal mining and reclamation, oversees state programs, restores abandoned mine lands, and protects communities and the environment from mining impacts.

agencies.name: Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA)
agencies.description: The Office of Textiles and Apparel analyzes trade in textiles and apparel, implements agreements and preference programs, and advises on policies that affect U.S. industry competitiveness and compliance with international textile rules.

agencies.name: Office of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology
agencies.description: The Office of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology coordinates Department of Transportation research, statistics, and technology policy, advances intelligent transportation systems, and aligns innovation with safety and infrastructure goals.

agencies.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
agencies.description: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency charters, regulates, and supervises national banks and federal branches and agencies of foreign banks to ensure safe, sound, and fair operations in the federal banking system.

agencies.name: Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI)
agencies.description: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence leads integration of foreign and domestic intelligence activities, sets enterprise priorities, and delivers all-source analysis to policymakers while overseeing community-wide security and oversight functions.

agencies.name: Office of the Federal Register (OFR)
agencies.description: The Office of the Federal Register publishes the Federal Register and Code of Federal Regulations, compiles laws in the United States Statutes at Large, and provides authenticated access to federal regulatory and legal documents.

agencies.name: Office of the Pardon Attorney
agencies.description: The Office of the Pardon Attorney reviews clemency petitions, investigates applicants’ records, and prepares recommendations so the President can exercise the pardon power fairly and consistently with governing legal standards.

agencies.name: Office of Weights and Measures (OWM)
agencies.description: The Office of Weights and Measures promotes uniformity in laws, regulations, and standards for weights and measures commerce, supports state enforcement programs, and helps ensure equity between buyers and sellers in the marketplace.

agencies.name: Office on Violence Against Women (OVW)
agencies.description: The Office on Violence Against Women awards grants and provides technical assistance to implement the Violence Against Women Act, strengthen criminal justice and victim services responses, and support prevention of gender-based violence.

agencies.name: Open World Leadership Center
agencies.description: The Open World Leadership Center administers congressional exchange programs that bring emerging leaders from participating countries to the United States for short-term professional delegations focused on accountable governance and civil society.

agencies.name: Peace Corps
agencies.description: The Peace Corps sends U.S. volunteers to partner countries for two-year assignments in education, health, agriculture, economic development, and youth engagement that build local capacity and advance mutual understanding between peoples.

agencies.name: Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC)
agencies.description: The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation insures defined benefit pensions in the private sector, pays benefits when plans fail within statutory limits, and promotes pension plan solvency through premiums and oversight.

agencies.name: Pentagon Force Protection Agency (PFPA)
agencies.description: The Pentagon Force Protection Agency provides law enforcement, physical security, and force protection for Pentagon facilities, personnel, and visitors in coordination with military and federal security partners in the National Capital Region.

agencies.name: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA)
agencies.description: The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration develops and enforces safety standards for pipelines and hazardous materials transportation, conducts inspections, and investigates incidents to reduce risk to people and the environment.

agencies.name: Postal Regulatory Commission
agencies.description: The Postal Regulatory Commission provides independent oversight of Postal Service rates, service standards, and financial transparency, reviews market-dominant and competitive product changes, and helps ensure statutory obligations are met.

agencies.name: President's Council on Fitness, Sports and Nutrition (PCSFN)
agencies.description: The President’s Council on Sports, Fitness and Nutrition promotes national awareness of physical activity and nutrition through partnerships, recognition programs, and public messaging aligned with federal dietary and activity guidelines.

agencies.name: Presidio Trust
agencies.description: The Presidio Trust is a federal corporation that stewards the Presidio of San Francisco as part of Golden Gate National Recreation Area, balancing historic preservation, environmental restoration, and revenue-generating leases that support the park.

agencies.name: Pretrial Services Agency for the District of Columbia
agencies.description: The Pretrial Services Agency for the District of Columbia supervises defendants on release, conducts risk assessments and drug testing, and provides reports and services that support fair and efficient pretrial justice in D.C. courts.

agencies.name: Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board (PCLOB)
agencies.description: The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board reviews counterterrorism and intelligence programs for privacy and civil liberties protections, conducts oversight investigations, and issues public recommendations to Congress and the executive branch.

agencies.name: Public and Indian Housing (PIH)
agencies.description: The Office of Public and Indian Housing administers public housing, Housing Choice Vouchers, and Native American housing programs that provide affordable rental assistance, modernize assisted housing, and support resident services and self-sufficiency.

agencies.name: Radio Free Asia (RFA)
agencies.description: Radio Free Asia is a congressionally funded nonprofit broadcaster that provides independent news, reporting, and digital content to audiences in Asian countries where access to free media is restricted or incomplete.

agencies.name: Radio Free Europe and Radio Liberty (RFE/RL)
agencies.description: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty is a congressionally funded media organization that produces independent journalism and multimedia reporting for audiences in countries where media freedom is limited or under threat.

agencies.name: Railroad Retirement Board (RRB)
agencies.description: The Railroad Retirement Board administers retirement, survivor, disability, unemployment, and sickness benefit programs financed by railroad employment taxes for railroad workers and their families under the Railroad Retirement Act.

agencies.name: Rehabilitation Services Administration (RSA)
agencies.description: The Rehabilitation Services Administration awards grants to state vocational rehabilitation agencies and supports demonstration projects that expand employment, independent living, and community inclusion for people with disabilities.

agencies.name: Risk Management Agency (RMA)
agencies.description: The Risk Management Agency administers the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation, develops actuarial sound policies with private insurers, and delivers risk management education to help agricultural producers withstand weather and market losses.

agencies.name: Rural Business-Cooperative Service
agencies.description: The Rural Business-Cooperative Service provides loans, loan guarantees, and grants to strengthen rural businesses, cooperatives, utilities, and economic development organizations that create jobs and build resilient local economies.

agencies.name: Rural Development
agencies.description: The Rural Development mission area delivers loans, loan guarantees, and grants across housing, business, and infrastructure programs that support essential services, economic opportunity, and quality of life in rural communities.

agencies.name: Rural Housing Service
agencies.description: The Rural Housing Service provides direct loans, loan guarantees, and rental assistance to develop affordable single-family and multifamily housing and community facilities that meet rural residents’ needs.

agencies.name: Rural Utilities Service (RUS)
agencies.description: The Rural Utilities Service finances electric, telecommunications, and water and waste infrastructure in rural areas through loans and grants that improve reliability, public health, and broadband access for unserved and underserved communities.

agencies.name: Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation (GLS)
agencies.description: The Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation operates and maintains the St. Lawrence Seaway as a safe, efficient waterway linking the Great Lakes and the Atlantic Ocean for navigation and related purposes.

agencies.name: Secret Service
agencies.description: The Secret Service protects national leaders, visiting dignitaries, and secured facilities, and investigates crimes against U.S. financial and payment systems to safeguard currency and critical infrastructure.

agencies.name: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
agencies.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission regulates securities exchanges, broker-dealers, investment advisers, and funds to protect investors, promote fair and orderly markets, and enforce disclosure and anti-fraud standards.

agencies.name: Selective Service System (SSS)
agencies.description: The Selective Service System maintains registration records and stands ready to classify and deliver personnel to the Armed Forces in a national emergency under laws governing who must register.

agencies.name: Small Business Administration (SBA)
agencies.description: The Small Business Administration expands access to capital, federal contracting, counseling, and disaster assistance so small businesses can start, grow, and recover while strengthening local economies.

agencies.name: Smithsonian Institution
agencies.description: The Smithsonian Institution operates museums, libraries, research centers, and the National Zoo as the nation’s largest museum, education, and research complex advancing scientific and cultural understanding.

agencies.name: Social Security Administration (SSA)
agencies.description: The Social Security Administration assigns Social Security numbers and administers retirement, survivors, and disability insurance and Supplemental Security Income for people who meet statutory eligibility requirements.

agencies.name: Social Security Advisory Board (SSAB)
agencies.description: The Social Security Advisory Board advises the President, Congress, and the Social Security Commissioner on the financial condition and policy of Social Security and Supplemental Security Income programs.

agencies.name: Southeastern Power Administration
agencies.description: The Southeastern Power Administration markets hydroelectric power from federal reservoirs to public bodies and other eligible customers across the southeastern United States under delegated authority.

agencies.name: Southwestern Power Administration
agencies.description: The Southwestern Power Administration markets hydroelectric power from federal dams to public utilities and other eligible customers across designated states in the South and Southwest.

agencies.name: State Justice Institute (SJI)
agencies.description: The State Justice Institute awards grants and supports initiatives that strengthen state courts, improve justice administration, and foster coordination between state and federal judicial systems.

agencies.name: Stennis Center for Public Service
agencies.description: The Stennis Center for Public Service develops leadership in young people preparing for public careers and provides training and professional development for Congress and congressional staff.

agencies.name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
agencies.description: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration advances public behavioral health by funding services, disseminating evidence, and guiding policy on substance use disorders, mental illness, and recovery supports.

agencies.name: Supreme Court of the United States
agencies.description: The Supreme Court of the United States is the final judicial authority in the federal system, reviewing lower-court judgments and exercising original jurisdiction in the narrow categories Congress assigns by law.

agencies.name: Surface Transportation Board (STB)
agencies.description: The Surface Transportation Board regulates and adjudicates railroad rates, mergers, line sales, and related surface transportation matters to implement federal economic and competition policy.

agencies.name: Susquehanna River Basin Commission (SRBC)
agencies.description: The Susquehanna River Basin Commission is an interstate-federal compact agency that plans and regulates water resources in the basin to balance environmental stewardship with sustainable development.

agencies.name: Tax Court
agencies.description: The United States Tax Court hears disputes over federal income, estate, and certain other taxes before additional payment is generally required, providing a judicial forum independent of the Internal Revenue Service.

agencies.name: Tennessee Valley Authority
agencies.description: The Tennessee Valley Authority is a corporate agency that provides public power, manages the Tennessee River system for navigation and flood control, and promotes regional economic development in its service area.

agencies.name: Transportation Security Administration (TSA)
agencies.description: The Transportation Security Administration secures the nation’s transportation systems, including civil aviation and other modes, to protect travelers, workers, and commerce from terrorist and security threats.

agencies.name: U.S. AbilityOne Commission
agencies.description: The U.S. AbilityOne Commission administers the AbilityOne Program to create employment for people who are blind or have significant disabilities through the supply of products and services to the federal government.

agencies.name: U.S. Access Board
agencies.description: The U.S. Access Board issues accessibility guidelines and standards for the built environment, transportation, telecommunications equipment, and electronic and information technology to implement federal disability requirements.

agencies.name: U.S. Africa Command
agencies.description: The U.S. Africa Command plans and conducts military operations and security cooperation with African partners to advance U.S. interests, regional stability, and collective defense capabilities across the continent.

agencies.name: U.S. Agency for Global Media
agencies.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media supervises independent, congressionally chartered international networks that provide news and information about the United States and the world to overseas audiences.

agencies.name: U.S. Air Force
agencies.description: The U.S. Air Force organizes, trains, and equips air and space forces to conduct global power projection, deterrence, air superiority, mobility, intelligence, and support in defense of the United States and its allies.

agencies.name: U.S. Air Force Reserve Command
agencies.description: The Air Force Reserve Command prepares Reserve Airmen who augment active forces with combat-ready units and specialized capabilities for contingency operations and homeland defense missions.

agencies.name: U.S. Arctic Research Commission (USARC)
agencies.description: The U.S. Arctic Research Commission recommends national Arctic research policy and promotes coordination among federal, state, academic, tribal, and international partners on Arctic science priorities.

agencies.name: U.S. Army
agencies.description: The U.S. Army organizes, trains, and equips land forces to conduct unified land operations, deter aggression, and fight and win the nation’s wars as part of the joint force.

agencies.name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
agencies.description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers delivers civil works, military engineering, and environmental services that strengthen national security, reduce flood risk, sustain water resources, and support navigation and recovery.

agencies.name: U.S. Botanic Garden
agencies.description: The United States Botanic Garden cultivates and displays plants to educate the public about horticulture, conservation, and the role of plants in ecosystems and human well-being.

agencies.name: U.S. Capitol Police
agencies.description: The United States Capitol Police protects the Capitol complex, safeguards Members of Congress, officers, staff, and visitors, and enforces federal law on Capitol grounds through patrol, investigation, and protective operations.

agencies.name: U.S. Capitol Visitor Center
agencies.description: The Capitol Visitor Center welcomes the public to the Capitol, orients visitors to Congress and the building’s history, and supports tours and educational programming under the direction of the legislative branch.

agencies.name: U.S. Census Bureau
agencies.description: The U.S. Census Bureau conducts the decennial census and ongoing surveys that produce official statistics on the nation’s population, housing, economy, and governments for public and private decision-making.

agencies.name: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM)
agencies.description: The U.S. Central Command plans and directs military operations across the Middle East, Central and South Asia, and surrounding waters to deter conflict, counter threats, and secure U.S. regional interests.

agencies.name: U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB)
agencies.description: The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board investigates catastrophic chemical incidents, identifies root causes, and issues recommendations to prevent future harm to workers and communities.

agencies.name: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)
agencies.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services adjudicates immigration and naturalization benefits, safeguards immigration integrity, and carries out humanitarian protection programs under federal immigration law.

agencies.name: U.S. Coast Guard (USCG)
agencies.description: The U.S. Coast Guard enforces maritime law, promotes safety and security on U.S. waters, conducts search and rescue, and protects the marine environment as an armed service within the Department of Homeland Security.

agencies.name: U.S. Commission of Fine Arts
agencies.description: The U.S. Commission of Fine Arts advises the federal government on design and aesthetics for the nation’s capital, national memorials, and certain federal properties and coinage programs.

agencies.name: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF)
agencies.description: The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom monitors religious freedom abroad, reports on violations, and recommends policy responses to the President, Secretary of State, and Congress.

agencies.name: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
agencies.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission regulates derivatives markets to promote transparency, integrity, and competition while protecting market participants from fraud, manipulation, and abusive practices.

agencies.name: U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims
agencies.description: The United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims reviews final Board of Veterans’ Appeals decisions on veterans’ benefits claims under the exclusive jurisdiction Congress has assigned to the court.

agencies.name: U.S. Courts of Appeal
agencies.description: The U.S. courts of appeals review trial-court and agency decisions to ensure federal law is correctly interpreted and applied, resolving most appeals in the federal judiciary below the Supreme Court.

agencies.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
agencies.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection safeguards U.S. borders by facilitating lawful trade and travel while enforcing immigration, customs, and agriculture laws at ports of entry and between them.

agencies.name: U.S. Cyber Command
agencies.description: U.S. Cyber Command plans and conducts cyberspace operations alongside joint and interagency partners to defend Department of Defense networks and support national security in and through cyberspace.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA)
agencies.description: The Department of Agriculture advances U.S. agricultural productivity, rural prosperity, nutrition assistance, conservation, forestry, and research to strengthen food systems and natural resources stewardship.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC)
agencies.description: The Department of Commerce promotes economic growth and innovation by supporting businesses, trade, technology standards, oceans and weather services, and reliable economic and demographic data.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Defense (DOD)
agencies.description: The Department of Defense provides military forces to deter war, protect national security, and defeat adversaries when directed, overseeing the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Space Force.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Education (ED)
agencies.description: The Department of Education fosters educational excellence and equal opportunity by administering federal student aid, enforcing civil rights in education, and supporting evidence-based improvement across states and schools.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)
agencies.description: The Department of Energy advances energy security, environmental responsibility, and scientific discovery by stewarding the nuclear weapons enterprise, managing national labs, and shaping energy and technology policy.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
agencies.description: The Department of Health and Human Services protects public health and provides essential human services through Medicare, Medicaid, public health agencies, biomedical research, and social service programs.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS)
agencies.description: The Department of Homeland Security safeguards the homeland from terrorism and manages border security, immigration enforcement, cybersecurity, disaster response, and critical infrastructure protection missions.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
agencies.description: The Department of Housing and Urban Development expands affordable housing, enforces fair housing law, and invests in community development to strengthen urban and rural neighborhoods.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ)
agencies.description: The Department of Justice enforces federal law, represents the United States in court, protects civil rights, and ensures the fair and impartial administration of justice across independent litigating components.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)
agencies.description: The Department of Labor enforces worker protections on wages, safety, benefits, and equal employment; administers job training and unemployment insurance; and produces labor market statistics for policymakers and the public.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of State (DOS)
agencies.description: The Department of State conducts U.S. diplomacy, negotiates treaties, manages embassies and consulates, and shapes foreign policy to advance national security, prosperity, and democratic values abroad.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI)
agencies.description: The Department of the Interior stewards federal lands and waters, upholds trust responsibilities to tribes and Alaska Natives, and conserves fish, wildlife, and cultural resources for future generations.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury
agencies.description: The Department of the Treasury maintains the nation’s fiscal strength by collecting revenue, managing federal finances and debt, enforcing financial crimes laws, and advancing economic and sanctions policy.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT)
agencies.description: The Department of Transportation invests in and regulates the safety and performance of aviation, highways, rail, transit, pipelines, and maritime systems that move people and goods nationwide.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)
agencies.description: The Department of Veterans Affairs delivers health care, benefits, memorial services, and transition support to veterans and their families as the federal government’s principal veterans agency.

agencies.name: U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC)
agencies.description: The U.S. Election Assistance Commission assists state and local election officials, issues voluntary voting-system guidelines, distributes HAVA funds, and collects data to improve election administration and security.

agencies.name: U.S. European Command (USEUCOM)
agencies.description: The U.S. European Command plans and conducts military operations across Europe, portions of the Middle East, and Eurasia alongside allies and partners to deter aggression and defend NATO and U.S. interests.

agencies.name: U.S. Fire Administration (USFA)
agencies.description: The U.S. Fire Administration, within the Federal Emergency Management Agency, supports the fire and emergency services community through training, data, education, and programs that reduce loss of life and property.

agencies.name: U.S. Fleet Forces Command (USFFC)
agencies.description: U.S. Fleet Forces Command generates Navy forces, oversees Atlantic readiness, and provides maritime capabilities to combatant commanders for homeland defense, deterrence, and global naval operations.

agencies.name: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS)
agencies.description: The U.S. Geological Survey is the nation’s primary natural-science agency for impartial data and research on geology, water, biology, energy, minerals, hazards, and environmental change.

agencies.name: U.S. House of Representatives
agencies.description: The U.S. House of Representatives is the lower chamber of Congress, where Members elected from states and territories introduce legislation, appropriate funds, and exercise oversight of the executive branch.

agencies.name: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
agencies.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement enforces customs, trade, and immigration laws through criminal investigations and civil enforcement to protect national security and public safety.

agencies.name: U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM)
agencies.description: The U.S. Indo-Pacific Command plans and executes operations across the Indo-Pacific alongside allies and partners to preserve a free and open region and deter coercion against U.S. interests.

agencies.name: U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC)
agencies.description: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation mobilizes private investment in developing countries through loans, insurance, equity, and technical assistance aligned with U.S. foreign policy and development goals.

agencies.name: U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC)
agencies.description: The U.S. International Trade Commission investigates imports’ effects on U.S. industries, advises on trade remedies, and provides independent analysis to Congress and the President on international trade issues.

agencies.name: U.S. Marine Corps
agencies.description: The U.S. Marine Corps provides rapidly deployable combined-arms forces that conduct expeditionary and amphibious operations worldwide as a separate service within the Department of the Navy.

agencies.name: U.S. Marshals Service (USMS)
agencies.description: The U.S. Marshals Service protects the federal judiciary, apprehends fugitives, transports prisoners, manages seized assets, and operates witness security programs in support of federal law enforcement.

agencies.name: U.S. Military Academy, West Point
agencies.description: The U.S. Military Academy educates and trains cadets in leadership, academics, and military skills to commission officers who serve the Army and the nation with character and competence.

agencies.name: U.S. Mint
agencies.description: The United States Mint manufactures circulating coinage, produces numismatic and bullion coins for collectors and investors, and safeguards the integrity of U.S. currency materials under Treasury policy.

agencies.name: U.S. Mission to the United Nations (USUN)
agencies.description: The U.S. Mission to the United Nations represents the United States at the U.N. and related agencies, negotiating positions and advancing U.S. foreign policy in multilateral diplomacy.

agencies.name: U.S. National Central Bureau - Interpol
agencies.description: The U.S. National Central Bureau, INTERPOL Washington, coordinates international law-enforcement cooperation between U.S. agencies and INTERPOL member countries on transnational crime and fugitive matters.

agencies.name: U.S. Navy
agencies.description: The U.S. Navy maintains maritime forces that project power from the sea, deter adversaries, secure sea lines of communication, and support joint operations in defense of U.S. interests worldwide.

agencies.name: U.S. Northern Command (USNORTHCOM)
agencies.description: U.S. Northern Command plans homeland defense and civil-support operations for North America, coordinates with Canada and Mexico, and aligns military assistance to civil authorities for designated contingencies.

agencies.name: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
agencies.description: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission licenses and inspects commercial nuclear power plants, fuel facilities, and medical and industrial uses of nuclear materials to protect public health and the environment.

agencies.name: U.S. Parole Commission
agencies.description: The U.S. Parole Commission decides parole, supervised release, and related matters for eligible federal and District of Columbia offenders under statutes governing release and reentry.

agencies.name: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
agencies.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office examines and grants patents, registers trademarks, and administers intellectual property policy that promotes innovation and protects consumers from confusion and fraud.

agencies.name: U.S. Postal Inspection Service
agencies.description: The U.S. Postal Inspection Service investigates crimes involving the mail, protects postal employees and customers, and enforces laws that safeguard the postal system from fraud and dangerous misuse.

agencies.name: U.S. Postal Service (USPS)
agencies.description: The United States Postal Service provides universal mail and package delivery service across the country as an independent establishment of the executive branch funded primarily by postal revenues.

agencies.name: U.S. Senate
agencies.description: The U.S. Senate is the upper chamber of Congress, where each state elects two Senators who confirm appointments, ratify treaties, try impeachments, and share legislative and oversight responsibilities with the House.

agencies.name: U.S. Sentencing Commission
agencies.description: The U.S. Sentencing Commission promulgates federal sentencing guidelines, collects sentencing data, and conducts research to inform Congress, courts, and the executive branch on federal crime and punishment policy.

agencies.name: U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM)
agencies.description: U.S. Southern Command conducts security cooperation and operations across Central and South America and the Caribbean with partner nations to counter transnational threats and protect U.S. regional interests.

agencies.name: U.S. Space Command
agencies.description: U.S. Space Command conducts operations in and from space, synchronizes joint space forces, and deters conflict while protecting U.S. and allied space capabilities essential to national security.

agencies.name: U.S. Special Operations Command
agencies.description: U.S. Special Operations Command oversees planning, readiness, and global employment of special operations forces from the military services under a unified command structure for sensitive missions.

agencies.name: U.S. Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM)
agencies.description: U.S. Strategic Command deters strategic attack against the United States and its allies, operates nuclear command and control, and integrates space and cyber capabilities assigned for global strike and deterrence missions.

agencies.name: U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA)
agencies.description: The U.S. Trade and Development Agency helps overseas project sponsors adopt U.S. solutions by funding feasibility studies, technical assistance, and reverse trade missions that open export opportunities.

agencies.name: U.S. Trade Representative
agencies.description: The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative develops and coordinates U.S. trade policy, negotiates agreements, and enforces trade commitments to open markets and defend American workers and businesses.

agencies.name: U.S. Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM)
agencies.description: U.S. Transportation Command directs global mobility operations, integrating air, land, and sea lift to move forces and sustainment for the joint force and supported civilian agencies.

agencies.name: U.S. Trustee Program
agencies.description: The U.S. Trustee Program oversees administration of federal bankruptcy cases, monitors parties and trustees, and combats fraud and abuse to preserve the integrity of the bankruptcy system.

agencies.name: Udall Foundation
agencies.description: The Morris K. Udall and Stewart L. Udall Foundation supports scholarship, conflict resolution, and Native Nations programs that strengthen environmental stewardship, collaborative decision-making, and leadership in public service.

agencies.name: Under Secretary for Political Affairs
agencies.description: The Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs directs regional and bilateral policy through the Department’s geographic bureaus and coordinates diplomatic strategy across crises and international institutions.

agencies.name: Under Secretary for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs
agencies.description: The Under Secretary for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs leads State Department efforts to explain U.S. policy abroad and engage foreign publics through strategic communication and educational exchange.

agencies.name: Unified Combatant Commands
agencies.description: Unified combatant commands integrate forces from multiple services under single commanders who plan and execute military operations across geographic regions or functional missions worldwide.

agencies.name: Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USU)
agencies.description: The Uniformed Services University educates and prepares uniformed health professionals and scientists who support the medical readiness of the Armed Forces and national health security missions.

agencies.name: United States Institute of Peace (USIP)
agencies.description: The United States Institute of Peace advances conflict analysis, mediation, and peacebuilding practice through research, training, and programs that help prevent and resolve violent conflict abroad.

agencies.name: Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA)
agencies.description: The Veterans Benefits Administration adjudicates claims for disability compensation, education, home loans, insurance, and other earned benefits and helps veterans access available support.

agencies.name: Veterans' Employment and Training Service (VETS)
agencies.description: The Veterans’ Employment and Training Service promotes veterans’ employment rights, funds transition services, and partners with employers and workforce agencies to connect veterans to meaningful careers.

agencies.name: Veterans Health Administration (VHA)
agencies.description: The Veterans Health Administration operates the nation’s largest integrated health system, delivering primary, specialty, and extended care to eligible veterans in facilities and through community partnerships.

agencies.name: Voice of America (VOA)
agencies.description: Voice of America provides accurate, objective news and information in multiple languages to global audiences on behalf of the United States as part of the U.S. Agency for Global Media network.

agencies.name: Wage and Hour Division (WHD)
agencies.description: The Wage and Hour Division enforces federal wage, hour, child labor, and family and medical leave laws to ensure workers receive lawful pay and protections in workplaces nationwide.

agencies.name: Washington Headquarters Services (WHS)
agencies.description: Washington Headquarters Services provides administrative, security, real-property, and support services that enable the Office of the Secretary of Defense and defense agencies in the National Capital Region.

agencies.name: Western Area Power Administration (WAPA)
agencies.description: The Western Area Power Administration markets hydroelectric power and transmission from federal projects to public utilities and other eligible customers across much of the central and western United States.

agencies.name: White House
agencies.description: The White House is the official residence and principal workplace of the President, housing the Executive Office of the President and supporting the chief executive’s conduct of national and international affairs.

agencies.name: Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (WTB)
agencies.description: The Wireless Telecommunications Bureau develops and implements Federal Communications Commission policies for wireless spectrum licensing, competitive markets, and technical rules governing mobile and fixed wireless services.

agencies.name: Women's Bureau
agencies.description: The Women’s Bureau leads Department of Labor policy on working women by researching labor issues, promoting equitable workplaces, and advancing programs that improve job quality and economic security.

agencies.name: Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars
agencies.description: The Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars is a nonpartisan institute that convenes research and dialogue on global policy questions to inform policymakers, scholars, and the public.
